why: Staples are near the bottom of archetype 1: +10.8 pct absolute, -20.5 pts excess, and they are the worst excess-return sector in policy-relief expansions (-19.6 pts). Their documented edge is in exogenous shocks and policy-pivot transitions, neither of which is the active mechanism (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix; Forward Test Pre-Registration, registered 2026-08-23).
The panel agrees on the month at -2.01 pts vs SPY, so the archetype prior and the arithmetic point the same way over the longer horizon (panel metrics, this file).
risks: The week reading is the opposite of the month: +1.13 pts vs SPY, rank 7 of 11. A defensive bid appearing in the same week the technician read is 'distribution' is worth watching as a regime signal rather than dismissing as noise (panel metrics, this file; wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).

why: Staples' weakness in expansions is a being-left-behind effect, not a fundamental impairment -- the sector posts positive excess return in archetypes 7 and 8, so this is a positioning call tied to the regime label holding (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix).

The consumer prints that would help Staples relatively (retail -0.6 pct, WMT comp miss, UMich 51.0) are the same ones that hurt Discretionary, so the pair is the cleaner expression than either leg alone (wiki/economic-calendar.md@63b4d3ba; wiki/synthesis.md@cd85b433).
risks: If the regime label is wrong and this is a late-cycle turn, the archetype-1 prior is exactly backwards for this sector -- Staples is the best relative performer in the recession case (The Full Regime-Sector Matrix).
